newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-SFE wheat in low-volume range trades.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-SFE wheat in low-volume range trades.

text.p: Australian wheat futures remained in their established price range in continued low-volume trading on Wednesday.
January 1997 rose by A$3.50 to A$164.00 in five trades while July 1997 surprised by trading five contracts at A$155.00, down A$2.50 on the trade.
Ben Suttie of C A & L Bell Commodities Corp Pty Ltd said longs in January were looking to take delivery, causing a drop in open interest positions in recent weeks.
The dominant influence in the Australian market remained the Australian Wheat Board pool price at A$185.00 a tonne, which continued to support the market.
When the pool was closed cash bids in Australia were likely to drop. But whether closure would occur next week was still not known, he said.
Chicago looked "toppy" but Argentina and Europe were becoming more expensive, so the U.S. was pricing itself in.
Old crop wheat may be reasonably well supported in the short-term, as was the new crop with low planting figures in the U.S., he said.
